criteria.name: Opening
criteria.description: Within the first two rep turns: says who they are, which company, and a specific reason for the call that is relevant to this buyer. Earns the next minute rather than asking for it.

criteria.name: Discovery questions
criteria.description: Asks open, specific questions about the buyer's situation, pain, and process before pitching. Follows up on answers instead of moving to the next scripted question.

criteria.name: Active listening
criteria.description: Reflects the buyer's own words back, builds the next question on what the buyer said, and lets the buyer finish. Does not steamroll or monologue.

criteria.name: Value articulation
criteria.description: States concretely what the product does and ties it to a pain or number the buyer has expressed. Generic claims ('increase sales', 'best-in-class') earn a 1 or 2.

criteria.name: Objection handling
criteria.description: When the buyer raises an objection: acknowledges it, asks a clarifying question or reframes, and answers with something specific. Ignoring, arguing, or caving immediately scores low.

criteria.name: Next step
criteria.description: Explicitly asks for a concrete next step with a time, participants, or agenda, and gives a reason it is worth the buyer's time.

criteria.name: Positioning
criteria.description: Differentiates against the buyer's status quo or incumbent (an existing tool, ride-alongs, doing nothing) and against price pressure, without disparaging competitors.

scenarios.title: Warm inbound: follow up on a demo request
scenarios.brief: Elena Ruiz, Director of Sales Enablement at Cartwheel, asked for a demo yesterday. Call her back, learn how she trains SDRs today, and book the demo.

scenarios.title: Cold call: VP Sales Ops at a freight brokerage
scenarios.brief: Priya Raghavan runs a 60-rep sales team at Meridian Logistics and did not ask for this call. Earn four minutes, find a real pain, and ask for a next step.

scenarios.title: Discovery: skeptical VP Engineering at a fintech
scenarios.brief: Marcus Bell, VP Engineering at Ledgerline (200-person fintech), booked 20 minutes on behalf of the VP of Sales. Run discovery on why new AEs take 7 months to ramp.

scenarios.title: Objections: RevOps leader who already has Gong
scenarios.brief: Dana Okafor runs RevOps for 80 sellers at Brightpath HR and renewed Gong five months ago. Handle her objections and position practice against post-call recording.

scenarios.title: Negotiation: CFO pushing back on a $48k quote
scenarios.brief: Sam Whitfield, CFO of Northwind Analytics, must approve a $48,000 annual deal for 40 reps and has a $35k ceiling. Defend the value, trade rather than cave, and set up a business-case review.

drills.title: The 30-second opener
drills.instructions: Write and say out loud an opener with your name, company, and one buyer-specific reason for calling in under 30 seconds. Re-run the cold call scenario using only that opener.

drills.title: Earn the next minute
drills.instructions: Practice ending your opener with a question about the buyer's world, not 'do you have a minute?'. Try three variants in a row.

drills.title: Five open questions
drills.instructions: Before your next roleplay, write five open questions about the buyer's process. Ask at least three before saying anything about your product.

drills.title: Follow the answer
drills.instructions: For every answer the buyer gives, ask one follow-up that uses a word they just said before changing topic.

drills.title: Reflect, then ask
drills.instructions: Start each of your turns by restating the buyer's last point in one sentence. Aim for three reflections in one call.

drills.title: Keep turns under 20 seconds
drills.instructions: Re-run a scenario with a hard rule: no turn longer than two sentences. Watch your longest-monologue metric drop.

drills.title: Tie value to their number
drills.instructions: Pick one number the buyer said (reps, ramp months, churn) and build one sentence that connects your product to it.

drills.title: No adjectives
drills.instructions: Describe what the product does without using 'best', 'powerful', 'seamless' or 'increase sales'. Say what it does and for whom.

drills.title: Acknowledge, ask, answer
drills.instructions: For each objection: acknowledge in one sentence, ask one clarifying question, then answer specifically. Practice on the Dana scenario.

drills.title: Trade, don't cave
drills.instructions: When price comes up, ask what would have to be true for the price to work before offering anything. Run the Sam scenario.

drills.title: Name the day
drills.instructions: End every call by proposing a specific day, time, and agenda for the next step. Do not accept 'send me an email' without one more ask.

drills.title: Give a reason to meet
drills.instructions: Pair your next-step ask with one sentence on what the buyer will get out of that meeting.

drills.title: Beat 'do nothing'
drills.instructions: Write two sentences on what the buyer loses by keeping their current approach. Use them when the buyer says they already have something.

drills.title: Position against the incumbent
drills.instructions: Name one thing the buyer's current tool does well, then the one thing it cannot do that you can. Practice on the Dana scenario.
